preview.title: How Depots and Releases Are Organised
preview.summary: Depot operations follow a shared local routine with site-specific adjustments, while releases are organised as a gated process with documented build and deploy steps. The available release notes do not detail all three gates.

content.text: The depot reports describe recurring, on-site operating routines, with changes made to address individual locations’ needs. The release notes instead describe a sequence of gates and specify tasks and owners for parts of the process.
Recurring local operations are reported by depot for May.
Every release goes through three gates.
Shift leads check loading bays, sorting belts and the returns desk each morning; drivers collect routes and scan parcels at the gate.
The documented build step compiles sources and runs unit tests. The deploy step restarts workers one at a time.
The reports describe shift leads, drivers and supervisors carrying out recurring local responsibilities.
The build and deploy steps have named owners: Alice for Build and Bob for Deploy.
Sites report different changes or constraints, including staffing changes, equipment or layout changes, weather disruptions, a vehicle recall and temporary packer training.
The available release notes specify build and deploy details, but do not describe the third gate.
Depot organisation: shared routines, local adjustments

Across the reports, daily work is organised around a repeated floor-and-dispatch routine: shift leads review key areas each morning, drivers collect routes from the dispatch office and scan parcels at the gate, and customers can track deliveries. Supervisors also write weekly summaries of delays.

The reports also record site-level differences rather than a single uniform response: Berlin added staff, Madrid added a sorting belt, Paris opened a loading dock, and Prague relocated its returns desk. Other reports note weather-related interruptions, a van recall or temporary packer training.
Release organisation: gates, tasks and named owners

The release process is framed as three gates. The available details describe Build—compiling sources and running unit tests—and Deploy, owned by Bob, which restarts workers one at a time. Alice is listed as the Build owner.

In short, depot organisation is described through repeated local routines and site-specific operating conditions. Release organisation is described through a gated sequence, with named owners and specific controls documented for Build and Deploy. The evidence does not establish how the depot model compares with release operations in terms of scale, governance or performance.
